Cheat sheet of **named teaching formulas** copied from the week notes. Worked numeric examples stay on the week pages. Word definitions stay in the [Glossary](glossary.qmd). Citeable programme numbers stay on [Key figures](key-figures.qmd).

- Keep **Sandbox ≠ Sandbox X**.
- **U-space ≠ Hong Kong law.**
- OHKF **HK$350bn** is a private think-tank **value-added** projection — not obtainable demand.
- Do **not** invent corridor capacity $K$.

## Week 1 — Value, GC, and entry {#week-01}

Full notes: [Week 1](week-01.qmd) · 8 identities below.

### Value of time saved {#w01-vot}

$$
\text{Value of time saved per trip} = \text{VOT} \times \Delta T
$$

Time saved on a trip valued at the customer’s value of time (VOT). [Value of time (VOT)](week-01.qmd#value-of-time-vot)

### Net present value (NPV) {#w01-npv}

$$
\text{NPV} = -\text{Initial investment} + \text{Present value of future profits}
$$

Whether future cash, after costs and risk, justifies what must be spent today. [Net present value (NPV)](week-01.qmd#net-present-value-npv)

### Annual operating profit {#w01-op-profit}

$$
\text{Annual operating profit} = \text{Annual revenue} - \text{Annual operating cost}
$$

Simple operating screen before discounting into NPV. [A three-step viability screen](week-01.qmd#a-three-step-viability-screen)

### Generalized cost (short form) {#w01-gc}

$$
\text{Generalized cost} = \text{Ticket price} + \text{VOT} \times \text{Travel time}
$$

Money plus time in one comparable burden for mode choice. [7. Generalized cost and mode choice](week-01.qmd#7-generalized-cost-and-mode-choice)

### Maximum fare against an alternative {#w01-pmax}

$$
P_{\max} = GC_A - \text{VOT}\times T_{\text{air}}
$$

Fare ceiling so air matches the alternative’s generalized cost. [How GC connects to VOT and to fare caps](week-01.qmd#how-gc-connects-to-vot-and-to-fare-caps)

### Ticket-price decomposition {#w01-ticket-share}

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Ticket price} =\ &\text{Aircraft cost} + \text{Vertiport fee} + \text{Energy} \\
&+ \text{UTM fee} + \text{Maintenance and labour} \\
&+ \text{Insurance and overhead} + \text{Operator margin}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Teaching split of who gets paid inside one fare — not a tariff schedule. [How a ticket price might be shared](week-01.qmd#how-a-ticket-price-might-be-shared)

### Entry-barrier sum {#w01-entry}

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Entry barrier} =\ &\text{Investment cost} + \text{Compliance cost} \\
&+ \text{Cost of delay} + \text{Uncertainty}.
\end{aligned}
$$

What a sandbox can change economically: cost, delay, and uncertainty — not a waiver of safety. Keep Sandbox ≠ Sandbox X. [Entry barriers as a simple sum](week-01.qmd#entry-barriers-as-a-simple-sum)

### Cost per passenger (unit cost) {#w01-unit-cost}

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Cost per passenger}
=\ &\text{Variable cost per passenger} \\
&+ \frac{\text{Daily fixed cost}}{\text{Flights per day}\times\text{Seats per flight}\times\text{Load factor}}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Fixed cost spread over filled seats; empty seats raise unit cost. [13. The empty-seat problem and unit cost](week-01.qmd#13-the-empty-seat-problem-and-unit-cost)

## Week 2 — Competition, cost, and co-opetition {#week-02}

Full notes: [Week 2](week-02.qmd) · 6 identities below.

### Herfindahl–Hirschman Index (HHI) {#w02-hhi}

$$
HHI = \sum_{i=1}^{N} s_i^2
$$

Concentration score from market shares; higher means more uneven. [Herfindahl–Hirschman Index (HHI)](week-02.qmd#herfindahl-hirschman-index-hhi)

### Average total cost per flight (ATC) {#w02-atc}

$$
\text{ATC} = \frac{\text{Fixed costs}}{\text{Number of flights}} + \text{Marginal cost}
$$

Fixed site cost spread over flights, plus marginal cost. [5. Fixed cost, marginal cost, and average cost per flight](week-02.qmd#5-fixed-cost-marginal-cost-and-average-cost-per-flight)

### Average cost with density {#w02-density}

$$
\text{Average cost per flight} = \frac{\text{Fixed route costs}}{\text{Flights} \times \text{Density factor}} + \text{Marginal cost}
$$

More volume through the same corridor and sites spreads fixed route cost. [6. Economies of density (not bigger vehicles)](week-02.qmd#6-economies-of-density-not-bigger-vehicles)

### Limit price / entrant average cost {#w02-limit}

$$
P_{\text{Limit}} \approx AC_{\text{Entrant}} = \frac{\text{Sunk entry cost}}{\text{Expected volume } Q} + MC
$$

Incumbent price low enough that entry looks unprofitable given sunk entry cost. [Limit pricing](week-02.qmd#limit-pricing)

### Bertrand price under unconstrained capacity {#w02-bertrand}

$$
P = MC \quad \text{(unconstrained capacity, homogeneous product)}
$$

With homogeneous service and spare capacity, undercutting can push price toward marginal cost. [Bertrand intuition](week-02.qmd#bertrand-intuition)

### Savings from sharing fixed infrastructure {#w02-share}

$$
\text{Savings per operator relative to going alone} = \frac{\text{Fixed infrastructure cost} \times (N-1)}{N}
$$

Split a shared fixed site cost among $N$ operators — only if access rules work. [10. Co-opetition: compete on service, share the roof](week-02.qmd#10-co-opetition-compete-on-service-share-the-roof)

## Week 3 — Unit cost, revenue, and breakeven {#week-03}

Full notes: [Week 3](week-03.qmd) · 7 identities below.

### Daily economic cost {#w03-daily-econ}

$$
\text{Daily economic cost}
=
\frac{\text{Asset cost} - \text{Expected residual value}}{\text{Useful operating days}}
+ \text{Daily OPEX}
$$

Net asset cost spread over useful days, plus that day’s operating spend. [A simple daily economic-cost approximation](week-03.qmd#a-simple-daily-economic-cost-approximation)

### CASK (cost per available seat-kilometre) {#w03-cask}

$$
CASK = \frac{\text{Operating cost for the period}}{\text{Available seats} \times \text{Kilometres flown}}
$$

Operating cost divided by seat-kilometres offered (sold or empty). [CASK (cost per available seat-kilometre)](week-03.qmd#cask-cost-per-available-seat-kilometre)

### Cost per mission-kilometre {#w03-mission-km}

$$
\text{Cost per mission-km}
=
\frac{\text{Operating cost for the period}}{\text{Total mission-kilometres}}
$$

Unit cost for cargo, inspection, emergency, or public-service missions. [Cost per mission-kilometre](week-03.qmd#cost-per-mission-kilometre)

### Revenue per flight {#w03-rev-flight}

$$
\text{Revenue per flight}
=
\text{Seats} \times \text{Load factor} \times \text{Average fare}
$$

Seats offered times share occupied times average fare — not “fill every seat.” [6. Revenue management (not “fill every seat”)](week-03.qmd#6-revenue-management-not-fill-every-seat)

### Breakeven units {#w03-be}

$$
\text{Breakeven units}
=
\frac{\text{Fixed cost}}{\text{Revenue per unit} - \text{Variable cost per unit}}
$$

Volume needed before contribution covers fixed cost. [7. Breakeven volume](week-03.qmd#7-breakeven-volume)

### Required missions per day {#w03-missions-day}

$$
\text{Required missions per day}
=
\frac{\text{Fixed daily cost}}{\text{Contribution margin per mission}}
$$

Daily activity target from fixed daily cost and contribution per mission. [7. Breakeven volume](week-03.qmd#7-breakeven-volume)

### Profit under a mixed-revenue sketch {#w03-mixed-profit}

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Profit} ={}& \text{Committed revenue} + \text{Usage revenue} + \text{Insurance payout} \\
&- \text{Fixed cost} - \text{Variable cost} - \text{Premiums and service credits}
\end{aligned}
$$

Committed + usage + insurance cash, minus fixed/variable cost and premiums/credits. [Profit under a mixed-revenue sketch](week-03.qmd#profit-under-a-mixed-revenue-sketch)

## Week 4 — Demand, GC, and elasticity {#week-04}

Full notes: [Week 4](week-04.qmd) · 9 identities below.

### Linear demand (classroom) {#w04-linear}

$$
Q = a - bP
$$

Expected quantity falls linearly as price rises. [Linear demand (classroom form)](week-04.qmd#linear-demand-classroom-form)

### Potential LAE passenger-trips {#w04-funnel}

$$
\text{Potential LAE passenger-trips}
=
\text{Relevant trips} \times \text{Corridor share} \times \text{Mode share}
$$

Relevant trips × corridor share × mode share — still before capacity. [Managerial demand funnel](week-04.qmd#managerial-demand-funnel)

### Served passenger-trips (capacity screen) {#w04-served-funnel}

$$
\text{Served passenger-trips}
=
\min\{\text{Potential demand},\ \text{Available capacity}\}
$$

Served trips cannot exceed available capacity. [Managerial demand funnel](week-04.qmd#managerial-demand-funnel)

### Generalized cost (door-to-door) {#w04-gc}

$$
GC = \text{Fare} + VOT \times \text{Door-to-door time} + \text{Other monetized burdens}
$$

Fare plus VOT × full door-to-door time, plus other monetized burdens. [5. Generalized cost and door-to-door comparison](week-04.qmd#5-generalized-cost-and-door-to-door-comparison)

### Own-price elasticity {#w04-ed}

$$
E_d = \frac{\%\ \text{change in quantity demanded}}{\%\ \text{change in price}}
$$

How much quantity moves when your own price changes. [6. Elasticity of demand](week-04.qmd#6-elasticity-of-demand)

### Total revenue across products {#w04-rev-sum}

$$
\text{Total revenue} = \sum_{i=1}^{n} P_i Q_i(P_i)
$$

Sum across products of each product’s price times its quantity. [7. Heterogeneity and differentiated products](week-04.qmd#7-heterogeneity-and-differentiated-products)

### Scenario demand with acceptance {#w04-accept}

$$
\text{Scenario demand} = \text{Base demand} \times \text{Acceptance adjustment}
$$

Base demand times an explicit acceptance factor you defend. [Transparent acceptance adjustment](week-04.qmd#transparent-acceptance-adjustment)

### Served quantity under shocks {#w04-qserved}

$$
Q_{\text{served}} = \min\{Q_{\text{demand}},\ Q_{\text{capacity}}\}
$$

Served activity is the minimum of demand and capacity. [9. Scenario analysis and shocks](week-04.qmd#9-scenario-analysis-and-shocks)

### Revenue under served quantity {#w04-r}

$$
R = P \times Q_{\text{served}} + \text{Committed revenue} - \text{Refunds and credits}
$$

Price × served quantity, plus committed revenue, minus refunds and credits. [9. Scenario analysis and shocks](week-04.qmd#9-scenario-analysis-and-shocks)

## Week 5 — Sites, capacity, and network cost {#week-05}

Full notes: [Week 5](week-05.qmd) · 6 identities below.

### Generalized site cost {#w05-site}

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Generalized site cost}
&= \text{Annualized infrastructure cost} \\
&\quad + \text{Annual OPEX} \\
&\quad + \text{Monetized access burden} \\
&\quad + \text{Expected disruption cost}
\end{aligned}
$$

Annualized build + OPEX + monetized access burden + expected disruption — a screening sum. [Generalized site cost (screening)](week-05.qmd#generalized-site-cost-screening)

### Breakeven capacity use {#w05-be-cap}

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Breakeven capacity use}
&=
\frac{\text{Fixed daily facility cost}}
{\text{Reliable daily capacity}
  \times \text{Contribution per movement}}
\end{aligned}
$$

Share of reliable capacity that must be used to cover fixed facility cost. [Breakeven capacity use](week-05.qmd#breakeven-capacity-use)

### Simple return screen {#w05-return}

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Simple return}
&=
\frac{\text{Adjusted revenue}
  - \text{Adjusted operating cost}}
{\text{Initial investment}}
\end{aligned}
$$

Rough return under reliability scenarios — not a full NPV. [6. Reliability scenarios (simple return screen)](week-05.qmd#6-reliability-scenarios-simple-return-screen)

### Daily infrastructure cost {#w05-daily-infra}

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Daily infrastructure cost}
&=
\frac{\text{CAPEX} - \text{Expected residual value}}
{\text{Useful operating days}} \\
&\quad + \text{Daily OPEX}
\end{aligned}
$$

Net CAPEX spread over useful days, plus daily OPEX. [Daily infrastructure cost (economic sketch)](week-05.qmd#daily-infrastructure-cost-economic-sketch)

### Illustrative peak slot fee {#w05-slot-fee}

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Slot fee}
&= \text{Base fee} \\
&\quad + \text{Congestion charge}
  \times
  \left(
    \frac{\text{Requests}}{\text{Available slots}}
  \right)
\end{aligned}
$$

Base fee plus a congestion term that rises with request pressure — teaching design, not a tariff. [Illustrative peak-pricing rule (design choice, not a regulation)](week-05.qmd#illustrative-peak-pricing-rule-design-choice-not-a-regulation)

### Network cost bundle and GC per trip {#w05-gc-trip}

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Network cost bundle}
&= \text{Network fixed cost}
  + \text{Network OPEX}
  + \text{Disruption cost} \\
\text{GC per trip}
&= \frac{\text{Network cost bundle}}{\text{Served trips}}
  + \text{Access burden per trip}
\end{aligned}
$$

Network costs per served trip, plus access burden per trip. [Generalized cost per served trip](week-05.qmd#generalized-cost-per-served-trip)

## Week 6 — Partnerships and payment rules {#week-06}

Full notes: [Week 6](week-06.qmd) · 5 identities below.

### Monthly economic profit {#w06-econ-profit}

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Monthly economic profit}
&= \text{Revenue} - \text{Cash OPEX} \\
&\quad - \text{Monthly asset-cost allocation}
  - \text{Partner payments}
\end{aligned}
$$

Revenue minus cash OPEX, asset-cost allocation, and partner payments. [Monthly economic-profit screen](week-06.qmd#monthly-economic-profit-screen)

### Usage-based revenue {#w06-ru}

$$
\begin{aligned}
R_U &= p \times q
\quad\text{(usage-based revenue)}
\end{aligned}
$$

Price times quantity — volume risk sits with the operator. [4. Usage vs availability payments](week-06.qmd#4-usage-vs-availability-payments)

### Availability-based component {#w06-ra}

$$
\begin{aligned}
R_A &= A - D + u \times q
\quad\text{(availability-based component)}
\end{aligned}
$$

Readiness fee minus performance deductions, plus optional usage term. [4. Usage vs availability payments](week-06.qmd#4-usage-vs-availability-payments)

### Expected project value (decision tree) {#w06-epv}

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Expected project value}
&=
\sum_s \Pr(s)
  \times \text{Payoff under the chosen action in state } s
\end{aligned}
$$

Probability-weighted payoff of the action you would choose in each state. [Decision-tree screen](week-06.qmd#decision-tree-screen)

### Shared facility cost per movement {#w06-facility}

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Fixed cost per movement}
&= \frac{\text{Fixed facility cost}}{\text{Total movements}} \\
\text{Shared facility cost per movement}
&= \text{Fixed cost per movement}
  + \text{Variable facility cost per movement}
\end{aligned}
$$

Allocated fixed facility cost per movement plus variable facility cost. [Facility cost per movement](week-06.qmd#facility-cost-per-movement)

## Week 7 — Readiness, trials, and risk cost {#week-07}

Full notes: [Week 7](week-07.qmd) · 7 identities below.

### Net readiness value {#w07-readiness}

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Net readiness value}
&= \text{Contribution earned during the lead period} \\
&\quad - \text{Additional compliance and launch cost}
\end{aligned}
$$

Contribution during a lead window minus the extra compliance/launch cost that bought it. [Value of earlier market readiness](week-07.qmd#value-of-earlier-market-readiness)

### Trial value {#w07-trial}

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Trial value}
&= \text{Expected avoided redesign and delay cost} \\
&\quad + \text{Value of better information}
  - \text{Trial cost}
\end{aligned}
$$

Avoided redesign/delay plus information value, minus trial cost. [Value of a controlled trial](week-07.qmd#value-of-a-controlled-trial)

### Compliance investment appraisal {#w07-comp}

$$
\begin{aligned}
V_{\mathrm{appr}} &= \Pr(\text{approval}) \times V_{\mathrm{proj}} \\
V_{\mathrm{net}} &= V_{\mathrm{appr}} - C_{\mathrm{comp}} \\
V_{\mathrm{comp}} &= V_{\mathrm{net}} - C_{\mathrm{delay}}
\end{aligned}
$$

Approval-probability × project value, then subtract compliance and delay cost. [Compliance investment appraisal](week-07.qmd#compliance-investment-appraisal)

### Expected loss {#w07-eloss}

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Expected loss}
&= \sum_j \Pr(\text{event } j)
  \times \text{Financial consequence}_j
\end{aligned}
$$

Sum of probability times financial consequence across events. [6. The safety case and risk cost](week-07.qmd#6-the-safety-case-and-risk-cost)

### Risk cost {#w07-risk-cost}

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Risk cost}
&= \text{Prevention and mitigation cost} \\
&\quad + \text{Insurance cost}
  + \text{Retained expected loss}
\end{aligned}
$$

Prevention/mitigation + insurance + retained expected loss. [6. The safety case and risk cost](week-07.qmd#6-the-safety-case-and-risk-cost)

### Daily coordination cost {#w07-coord}

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Daily coordination cost}
&= \text{Fixed system cost} \\
&\quad + q \times \text{Variable digital cost} \\
&\quad + h \times \text{Human oversight cost}
\end{aligned}
$$

Fixed system + variable digital per operation + human oversight. **U-space ≠ Hong Kong law.** [7. U-space, UTM, and coordination cost](week-07.qmd#7-u-space-utm-and-coordination-cost)

### Weighted pathway score {#w07-score}

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Weighted score}
&= \sum_k w_k s_k
\end{aligned}
$$

Documented weights times pathway scores — not “approval time ÷ invented stringency.” [Regulatory-pathway scorecard](week-07.qmd#regulatory-pathway-scorecard)

## Week 8 — Congestion, slots, and roadmap NPV {#week-08}

Full notes: [Week 8](week-08.qmd) · 4 identities below.

### Marginal congestion cost (MCC) {#w08-mcc}

$$
\begin{aligned}
S_{\mathrm{delay}} &= \sum_j \left( D_j \times v_j \right) \\
\mathrm{MCC} &= S_{\mathrm{delay}} + C_{\mathrm{other}}
\end{aligned}
$$

External delay cost across affected users, plus other incremental costs. Do not invent corridor $K$. [Marginal congestion cost (illustrative)](week-08.qmd#marginal-congestion-cost-illustrative)

### Maximum affordable slot payment {#w08-bmax}

$$
B_{\max} = R_{\Delta} - C_{\Delta} - \pi_{\mathrm{req}}
$$

Incremental revenue minus incremental cost minus required contribution. [Maximum affordable slot payment](week-08.qmd#maximum-affordable-slot-payment)

### Coordination-cost saving {#w08-sday}

$$
S_{\mathrm{day}} = C_{\mathrm{legacy}} - C_{\mathrm{interop}}
$$

Daily net saving of interoperable process versus legacy coordination. [Coordination-cost savings](week-08.qmd#coordination-cost-savings)

### Phased roadmap NPV {#w08-npv}

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{CF}_{t}
&= I_{t} - O_{t} \\
\mathrm{NPV}
&= \sum_{t=0}^{T}
  \frac{\mathrm{CF}_{t}}{(1+r)^{t}}
\end{aligned}
$$

Incremental cash flows discounted over the roadmap horizon. [Phased roadmap value](week-08.qmd#phased-roadmap-value)

## Week 9 — Funnel, contribution, and scenarios {#week-09}

Full notes: [Week 9](week-09.qmd) · 4 identities below.

### Market funnel with capacity {#w09-funnel}

$$
\begin{aligned}
SAM
&= TAM \times e \\
D_{\mathrm{pot}}
&= SAM \times s \\
D_{\mathrm{served}}
&= \min\{D_{\mathrm{pot}},\, K\}
\end{aligned}
$$

TAM → SAM → potential demand → served after capacity $K$. OHKF HK$350bn is **value-added only** — not obtainable demand. [Market funnel with capacity](week-09.qmd#market-funnel-with-capacity)

### Daily revenue and contribution {#w09-contrib}

$$
\begin{aligned}
R_{\mathrm{day}}
&= D_{\mathrm{served}} \times p \\
\Pi_{\mathrm{var}}
&= R_{\mathrm{day}} - D_{\mathrm{served}} \times v
\end{aligned}
$$

Served demand × price, then minus variable cost of served units. [Revenue and contribution](week-09.qmd#revenue-and-contribution)

### Expected profit across scenarios {#w09-ev}

$$
\begin{aligned}
E[\Pi]
&= \sum_{s} \Pr(s)\, \Pi_{s}
\end{aligned}
$$

Probability-weighted profit (or other payoff) across scenarios. [Expected value and downside risk](week-09.qmd#expected-value-and-downside-risk)

### Hedonic log-price specification (illustrative) {#w09-hedonic}

$$
\begin{aligned}
\ln(P_{i})
&= \alpha + \beta N_{i} + \gamma A_{i} + \delta X_{i} + \varepsilon_{i}
\end{aligned}
$$

Log price on noise and other attributes — classroom tool, not a Hong Kong estimate. [Illustrative specification](week-09.qmd#illustrative-specification)

## Week 10 — Noise, privacy, emissions, and public service {#week-10}

Full notes: [Week 10](week-10.qmd) · 5 identities below.

### Efficient noise charge (benchmark) {#w10-noise}

$$
\begin{aligned}
C^{*}_{\mathrm{noise}}
&= \mathrm{MEC}_{\mathrm{noise}}
\end{aligned}
$$

Economic benchmark: charge equals marginal external noise cost — not a published CAD tariff. [Pricing a noise externality (economic benchmark)](week-10.qmd#pricing-a-noise-externality-economic-benchmark)

### Privacy-control cost {#w10-priv}

$$
\begin{aligned}
C_{\mathrm{priv}}
&= F_{\mathrm{gov}} + q \times v + A
\end{aligned}
$$

Governance fixed cost + variable processing × volume + audit/incident cost. [Privacy-control cost](week-10.qmd#privacy-control-cost)

### Operational electricity emissions {#w10-eop}

$$
\begin{aligned}
e_{\mathrm{op}}
&= E_{\mathrm{kWh}} \times f_{\mathrm{grid}}
\end{aligned}
$$

kWh per operation times grid emissions factor. Electric ≠ zero life-cycle emissions. [Electricity-related (operational) emissions](week-10.qmd#electricity-related-operational-emissions)

### Life-cycle emissions per functional unit {#w10-efu}

$$
\begin{aligned}
e_{\mathrm{FU}}
&= \frac{E_{\mathrm{v}} + E_{\mathrm{b}} + E_{\mathrm{i}} + E_{\mathrm{o}} + E_{\mathrm{e}}}{U}
\end{aligned}
$$

Vehicle + battery + infrastructure + operations + end-of-life, divided by lifetime use. [Life-cycle emissions per functional unit](week-10.qmd#life-cycle-emissions-per-functional-unit)

### Net contribution after public-service commitment {#w10-ps}

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Pi_{\mathrm{net}}
&= Q_{C}\, m_{C} + P_{\mathrm{PS}} - Q_{P}\, c_{P} - F
\end{aligned}
$$

Commercial contribution + public-service payment − public-service cost − fixed cost. [Funding a public-service commitment](week-10.qmd#funding-a-public-service-commitment)

## Week 11 — Viability recommendation {#week-11}

Full notes: [Week 11](week-11.qmd) · 1 identities below.

### Operating viability test {#w11-viability}

$$
\begin{aligned}
D_{\mathrm{served}}
&= \min\{D,\, K\} \\
\Pi_{\mathrm{op}}
&= (p - v)\, D_{\mathrm{served}} - F
\end{aligned}
$$

Served activity is $\min\{D,K\}$; operating profit is contribution minus fixed cost. Week 12 reapplies the same identity under exam shocks. [The viability test](week-11.qmd#the-viability-test)

## Week 12 — Networks, digital coordination, and leasing {#week-12}

Full notes: [Week 12](week-12.qmd) · 3 identities below.

### Possible undirected links {#w12-links}

$$
\begin{aligned}
L
&= \frac{N(N-1)}{2}
\end{aligned}
$$

Counts possible pairs among $N$ nodes — not scheduled routes, demand, or network value. [Counting possible connections](week-12.qmd#counting-possible-connections)

### Digital-coordination net saving {#w12-snet}

$$
\begin{aligned}
S_{\mathrm{net}}
&= C_{\mathrm{legacy}} - C_{\mathrm{dig}} - C_{\mathrm{trans}}
\end{aligned}
$$

Legacy cost minus digital process cost minus transition cost. [Digital-coordination business case](week-12.qmd#digital-coordination-business-case)

### Lessor leasing appraisal {#w12-lease}

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{CF}_{L,t}
&= R_{t} - F_{t} - M_{t} - I_{t} - L_{t} \\
\mathrm{NPV}
&= -P_{0}
  + \sum_{t=1}^{T}
    \frac{\mathrm{CF}_{L,t}}{(1+r)^{t}}
  + \frac{V_{T}}{(1+r)^{T}}
\end{aligned}
$$

Lease cash flows and residual value — leasing reallocates risk; it does not erase it. [Leasing appraisal (risk does not disappear)](week-12.qmd#leasing-appraisal-risk-does-not-disappear)
